title: Loads and Loading Limits on a Mountain Dining Plans Plan
content:
Money is loaded onto a plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range only while the plan record stands in the enrolled, active or exhausted state. Later loads must reach the plan's top-up minimum, and no load may take the balance above the plan's ceiling or the season's total above the plan's season limit; a load that would do either is refused rather than trimmed. Where the plan offers it, the household may set an automatic top-up that presents the plan's top-up amount whenever the balance falls below its trigger, and a top-up that is refused stops spending until it is settled.

## The state the plan must stand in

The state is taken from the collective's own record of the plan, as that record stands before the load, and not from the household's account of it. A plan standing in the enrolled, active or exhausted state takes a load; standing in any other state it does not, since those three are the only states in which money is loaded.

## The two limits a load is measured against

| Limit | What is measured against it | Where it is passed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The plan's top-up minimum | the amount of this load, on a plan that has already had its first load | the load is not taken |
| The plan's balance ceiling | the balance the plan would stand at once this load had cleared | the load is refused in whole |
| The plan's season limit | the loads already cleared on the plan in the season it is sold for, together with this load | the load is refused in whole |

Refused in whole means what it says: where a load would carry the balance or the season's total past its limit, none of that load is taken, and no smaller part of it is taken in its place.

## Boundary readings on hypothetical figures

Take a plan whose top-up minimum is $50.00 and which is already in use. A later load of $50.00 reaches the minimum and is taken. A later load of $49.00 falls short of it and is not.

Take a plan whose balance ceiling is $2500.00, standing at $2400.00. A load of $100.00 would leave the balance at $2500.00, which is not above the ceiling, so it is taken. A load of $101.00 would leave the balance at $2501.00, above the ceiling, so it is refused, and $100.00 of it is not taken in its place.

## The automatic top-up

A household may set an automatic top-up only on a plan offered with one. Once set, it presents the plan's top-up amount whenever the balance falls below the plan's trigger balance. A top-up that is refused stops spending on the plan until it is settled.
